RES.R@1E9830:
Thank you for using Indenco Net.

As a service to all our subscribers, we provide information only a local network can offer.
RES.R@1ED484:
Without further ado: to improve our network services further, we are conducting a survey.

Please answer the three questions below. Everyone who responds will receive a small gift.
RES.R@1F10D8:
Q1) Have you felt uneasy lately?
(Yes / No / Not sure)
Q2) Have people close to you changed?
(Yes / No / Not sure)
Q3) Have you seen anything strange?
(Yes / No / Not sure)
Please reply by mail.
RES.R@1F5030:
Long time no see. It's Fujita, your old classmate.
We haven't met since you and your family left the City after graduation.
I heard you were back and wanted to get in touch sooner. I found your office's mail address in the paper.
How are you?
RES.R@1F8C84: Same as ever here. My leg hasn't gotten any better. My father died about five years ago, and I moved to the west side of the City; the old house was too big for one. Now I use his money to carry on my "research." And I need your advice about it.
RES.R@1FC8D8: It must seem sudden after so many years, but I can only talk about this with someone I trust. And to me, you're still the only one. Something terrible is happening near the power plant. The "change" is fast! I'm always home. Call me. Better yet, come over!
RES.R@200830:
It's Fujita, your old classmate. Did you read the mail I sent before?

The strange happenings go on. Can you come over soon? Something is going on at the power plant south of my house. You're the only one I can count on!
RES.R@204830: It's Fujita, your old classmate. I got your mail. So you went to the power plant alone. About the monster you saw... honestly, I can't believe it. If anyone but you told me that, I'd lecture them for hours on "thinking scientifically."
RES.R@208484: ...Joking aside, something terrible did happen at the plant. Or rather, it isn't over yet. I have a special device here, and the data says the anomaly is still going on. The blue device in the basement you mentioned...
RES.R@20C0D8: ...is probably behind it. From the shape you described, it sounds like a kind of field converter. Could you take me to that basement? I'm usually home. I want to show you my experiments too, so come visit. No, not "visit." This matters more!
RES.R@210030: How are you holding up? The City keeps getting stranger. So much weirdness that it all starts to feel unreal, like a dream. A really nasty one, probably. By the way, in that cave under the power plant...
RES.R@213C84: ...remember the device I picked up? I thought it felt like a weapon, and it is: a powerful electromagnetic weapon. Think of a strong microwave oven with a tight beam, made small. The principle isn't hard, but this power at this size is amazing.
RES.R@2178D8: No civilian has tech like this. It was unfinished, but I got it working. In a test it punched through 50mm of steel instantly. If whoever builds things like this is behind the City's anomaly, we'd better arm ourselves too. I want you to have one. Come over!
RES.R@21B830:
How are you? The police haven't acted on the plant incident either. Someone is covering up what's happening in the City. If you find out what's going on, let me know.

I gave you the EM-wave gun, right? It's more than that.
RES.R@21F484: There was a part I removed, thinking it didn't matter. It turned out to be crucial. This thing is incredible, like something from science fiction. I couldn't believe it's possible. I found out by chance, checking the removed part's resistance.
RES.R@2230D8: We all live under Earth's gravity, right? But nobody truly knows what gravity is. Yet whoever built this weapon seems to know its basic principle. With it, you could take on even a giant like the one in the seaside warehouses.
RES.R@226D2C: It finally started working this morning. Maybe it's my adjustments, but it won't hit every time. Still, I think it's usable. I want you to have it. Come and get it, fast! There's no one else to count on. Somehow, save the City!
RES.R@22B030: This is Yamamoto from the thermal power plant. Thank you so much for the other day. I reported it to the police afterward. For an incident that serious, only three officers came. Even with bodies right in front of them, it looked like a box-ticking inspection.
RES.R@22EC84:
The creatures' bodies in the basement were gone, too, and the police didn't believe me.

Is that sort of thing "common"?

For now, I'm working to get the plant running again.
RES.R@233030: This mail should reach you by an unusual route. I am in danger myself, so I have no other way. I cannot reveal who I am, but I work for the government. My superiors will contact you.
RES.R@236C84: Or perhaps you have already met my successor. If so, you can guess who I am. For my own reasons, I have cut contact with my superiors. Nor can I leave where I am. Not that I am being held.
RES.R@23A8D8: I simply don't want to make things worse by leaving. Here is information on the seaside warehouses. In the City's southwest, two big brick warehouses stand around the docks. They have six entrances in all, and those six connect inside.
RES.R@23E52C: The two warehouses stand with the sea between them, so you may wonder what "connect inside" means. Take it literally. Each of the six entrances has a security system. Disable them, and destroy what's inside.
RES.R@242830: Forgive this first mail. My name is Sakaguchi, of the congregation of the cathedral in the Old Town. I always read your column in the local pages. You seem a person of sound judgment, so I am writing to you. Recently...
RES.R@246484: ...something has been happening at the cathedral. Several members of the congregation are missing, including elderly people who could hardly travel far. Their families have reported them to the police, but nothing has been found.
RES.R@24A0D8: I hate to think it, but the church is involved. I asked a priest I am close to, but he was distant, as if hiding something. Could the newspaper look into it? I go to the cathedral whenever I have time.
RES.R@24E030:
This is the congregation of the cathedral in the Old Town.

It was a terrible affair, but with the congregation at its heart, we hope the whole community can rebuild the church together.
RES.R@251C84:
At the police station, autopsies were done on those from the bell tower, and we went to identify what was taken from their stomachs.

We found belongings of a congregation member we had been close to.
RES.R@256030:
This is the congregation of the cathedral in the Old Town.

Four priests were murdered at the cathedral. The culprit is unknown. A sinful, terrible thing. People keep vanishing from the congregation. Everyone is shaken.
RES.R@259C84: Some even speak the two forbidden words of this church: "the End." Now, of all times, the old priest at the heart of our church has vanished. It seems he has shut himself in the crypt. The four murdered priests held the secret key to it.
RES.R@25D8D8: I will tell you about the crypt as a special case. Its very existence is not to be told to outsiders, but I hope you can help. The crypt is said to have another, hidden entrance. Beneath the City, an ancient underground waterway...
RES.R@26152C: ...runs in every direction, and they say it has a way in. Several buildings are also said to connect to this waterway. I've even heard it connects to the base of a group calling themselves psychics. If you learn anything, please tell me.
RES.R@265830: This is the Forest Rangers. A few days ago, strange lights were seen on the mountain north of the City. It isn't really our job, but I'm looking into it out of personal interest. I've found six witnesses, but their memories are vague. I can't tell when it happened.
RES.R@269484: Putting their stories together, a powerful glowing object fell, and the mountain shone for hours afterward. It could be a meteorite or special lightning, but might it be a UFO? I think it came down northwest of the home of Mr. Yamasaki, the mine owner.
RES.R@26D0D8:
An old man lives alone nearby, but he says he saw nothing. Has the paper had any other reports? I'd be grateful if you could tell me anything you find out.
(Personally, I'm hoping it was aliens...)
RES.R@271030:
This is the Forest Rangers.

I mailed you about the strange lights on the mountain north of the City. ...An update. I still haven't found where the meteorite (or UFO) fell. I don't want another Roswell, so I haven't told the police or the army.
RES.R@274C84: I think it fell on the land of the old man who lives alone, the one I said saw no lights. He knows something. I went to talk to him, but he threatened me with a gun. And it's suspicious that he was in hospital for days after the lights.
RES.R@2788D8: Could you meet him somehow, as a newspaper interview? He might let something slip to a reporter. If you find anything out, please tell me.
RES.R@27C830: This is the Forest Rangers. I found an alien! I went to the old man's house on the mountain that I told you about. The front door happened to be open, so I went in. There was a strange smell, so I went down to the basement, and there!
RES.R@280484: I found the body of a grotesquely deformed alien. It was wearing the old man's hat. The old man must have been eaten. A huge discovery! Please put it on the front page.
RES.R@284830:
Thank you for using Indenco Net. And thank you for taking part in our recent survey. Its results will shape how we run the network.

By the way, around you...
RES.R@288484:
...have strange things been happening? Something has crept into the City. It is eating away at all of you from the inside.

Indenco was founded to support your healthy development.
RES.R@28C0D8: Beware the "virus." It brings about distorted development.
RES.R@290030: Thank you for using Indenco Net. To dispel the unease spreading in the City, we will, as a special measure, give you proper information. Your consciousness is made of a part continuous with the cosmos and a part bounded by the body.
RES.R@293C84: In the City's anomaly, the walls of the individual part of consciousness are being torn down. This resembles a step written into the system called "evolution." But the "thing" that crept into the City is using this step to spread itself across the universe.
RES.R@2978D8: Forced evolution distorts the minds and bodies of you, its hosts. In the middle stages there may be painful, frightening deformation, and unnatural merging or splitting of personalities. We want only a healthy "evolution."
RES.R@29B830: Thank you for using Indenco Net. We will give you proper information. Many of you, we believe, have already begun to "change." But please do not be afraid.
RES.R@29F484: The thing that crept "inside" you carries only the minimum orders for survival. Those orders are: "Change, multiply, devour this planet, and fly off to the next." Most of your personality and knowledge will not be lost.
RES.R@2A30D8:
Do not blindly obey this "order" that speaks from within. That alone can greatly delay the "change." Be careful.
"Change!
Multiply!
Fill the universe!"
RES.R@2A7030:
This time we must give you sad news. Indenco too has finally been "interfered with." Things have changed.

"The door has been opened."

From now on, Indenco Network opens the upper floors of its headquarters.
RES.R@2AAC84: Information disclosed to Earth through the Indenco Interspecies Network will, under interplanetary agreement, be limited so as not to hinder its healthy development.
RES.R@2AF030:
We will give all needed information to those who come to us. As one of your planet's guides once said:
"Choose the narrow gate."
RES.R@2B3030: This is not a routine message. It's urgent. The Defense Bureau made an unusual request to the paper, and we'll cooperate fully. We weren't told clearly what it involves, only two things: that the nation is in crisis, and that it began in your City.
RES.R@2B6C84:
It's apparently a Level 1 national secret. The Defense Bureau should call you. Follow their instructions.

...That's the official line. What's going on there? Every road into the City is sealed. Each has some excuse, like road works...
RES.R@2BA8D8: ...or something more plausible. I've never heard of a Level 1 secret. An epidemic? A failed government experiment? Could this be one heck of a scoop?
RES.R@2BE830:
Another urgent message. The Defense Bureau called to confirm. They want you to meet a Bureau man named Kouda at Grand Station by noon today.

Get us that scoop.
RES.R@2C2830: The Seasons Hotel you recommended is very comfortable, and handy for gathering information. I've checked every likely place since, but found nothing. The three who came before me all erased their trails and vanished. Still, there's a reason I can't search...
RES.R@2C6484:
...on a large scale. That's why I need your help. Come to the hotel.

It's a nice hotel, but I can't shake the feeling I'm being watched. That's my specialty, yet I can't catch them.
RES.R@2CA830:
Did this mail reach you? The phones in the City are dead. This network seems the only way left to talk.

Since then I got out over the mountains. Met some very strange things on the way. Based on my report...
RES.R@2CE484:
...the government has secretly decided to send in the army. Hold out a little longer.

If this all ends safely, I'll stay at the Seasons Hotel again. Next time privately, with my wife.
RES.R@2D2830: It's been so long. Not since high school, right? I didn't write after I married, but you're back in the City! Fujita told me, and I was so surprised. Actually, I'm back too. Only for two weeks this time, though. A lot has happened since then...
RES.R@2D6484:
...and I'm thinking of living in the City. This trip I'm looking for work, and I'd like to find a place to live too.

I'm staying at the Seasons Hotel. Remember? "Our hotel"... right?
RES.R@2DA0D8:
Fujita says your office is very close by?

If you can, I'd love to see you. Dinner at the hotel tomorrow night? That restaurant hasn't changed. I'll call you tomorrow, sometime between afternoon and evening.
RES.R@2DE030: How are you? The hotel has calmed down a lot. The hospital job I mentioned, at New Town Public Hospital, looks like it's happening. It really starts next month, but the City's in such a state and they're short-handed, so I'm starting now as a temp.
RES.R@2E1C84: I don't even have my white coat yet. Everyone at the hospital seems to think it's a new kind of "infectious disease." No one badly "changed" has come in yet. But are people like the ones at the hotel just "sick"?
RES.R@2E6030: I waited for you at the hotel, but you didn't come. That's a shame. I wasn't hoping to go back to how things were. I just wanted to talk as old friends. From now on, let's each take good care of our own lives.
RES.R@2EA030: Nice to meet you. My name is Kuchiki, and I work at the Seasons Hotel. I had no one to talk to, so I found you in the paper. Something strange is happening at the hotel. Police keep coming and going, and it's full of odd people. They told us a guest had a notifiable disease...
RES.R@2EDC84:
...but I don't think that's it.

If you can, would you come to the hotel?
RES.R@2F2030:
This is Kuchiki from the Seasons Hotel. Thank you so much for the other day.

Please come by any time. You're welcome to stay with us whenever you like.
RES.R@2F6030: My name is Yuuki, a doctor at New Town Public Hospital. For several days, patients with a strange illness have been brought in. Their bodies deform rapidly. Unlike cancer and other abnormal growth, it seems to follow some law. There are infections in the hospital, even doctors...
RES.R@2F9C84:
...so it is clearly contagious. But we haven't found how it spreads.

Judging by how fast it spreads, there may be a great many patients across the City.

Please report on this in the paper.
RES.R@2FD8D8: And tell people to contact the public hospital right away if anything is wrong.
RES.R@301830: This is Suzuura, administrator of the Yamasaki Mine. The mine office has sent a strange report. As you know, the Yamasaki Mine has been closed for ten years. Apart from a few staff, no one goes in, and there's nothing inside anyway.
RES.R@305484: For three years now, no one, not even the caretakers, has gone deep inside. Yet in the past few days we've caught some fifty people coming out. We told the police, but none of them will say a word. All ages, men and women...
RES.R@3090D8: ...and they don't seem to have gone in for any reason. From children to old women. We tightened security, but though no one goes in, people keep coming out. I went to the mine yesterday, and all who came out seemed to be in a daze.
RES.R@30CD2C:
There are so many, with no clear motive, that we're at a loss how to deal with them.

Has the newspaper heard anything?
RES.R@311030: The Yamasaki family who owned the Yamasaki Mine are in big trouble. The mine's changed hands, and they're digging up everything under it. The mine goes deep underground. They fired us, and now they're up to something!
RES.R@315030:
We are the society of psychics, the Temple of Universe, T.O.U.

We have seen that a crisis approaches the City, and that you are the key person.

Beneath the City lies a labyrinth built by an ancient race.
RES.R@318C84:
This labyrinth connects to the basement of our society, the cathedral's underground waterway, the hospital, and the coal mine.

Please come to our society. We will be your guide.

RES.R@32201C: Agent Kouda | Meet me at the hotel
RES.R@32281C: Naomi | I'm back in the City!
RES.R@32381C: Kuchiki Ayumu | Thank you very much
